commands.summary: 265 tests passed. New/updated coverage for Phase 3.1: (Finding 1) event-type/direction compatibility -- inbound fax.failed deferred without local outbound lookup even when its provider_fax_id matches an existing outbound fax; outbound fax.failed still resolves normally; outbound-only event type claiming inbound direction (and the inverse) fails closed as event_direction_mismatch before any resolution attempt; a genuine local identity mix-up (outbound-routable event resolving to a local fax of the wrong direction) still fails closed via the retained direction_mismatch guard; the old test that conflated these two failure modes was replaced, not merely patched. (Finding 2) an outbound fax.failed event's failure_category propagates to both faxes.failure_category and the fax_events ledger row; internal_failure_reason never appears in either table or the ingress row; fax.delivered's bounded page_count propagates to the canonical fax record; a non-failure observation never carries a stale prior failure category forward; a stale earlier observation cannot overwrite the authoritative state, page_count, or failure category (but is still durably ledgered). (Finding 3) a fresh transient media URL remains available before its ~10 minute expiry; an expired one is cleared while the rest of the ingress record (including deferred_inbound status, page_count, event identity) survives; clearing never touches outbound fax/document rows; a simulated restart clears an already-expired URL; envelope parsing derives the expiry from occurred_at, never fabricating one when no media_url is present. (Finding 4) unresolvedTelnyxFaxWebhookEventsPage walks a 130-row unresolved backlog exactly once via a stable rowid cursor in a bounded number of pages; a full server.ts createBackend startup sweep against a 150-row backlog resolves a previously-unresolved event at index 120 (beyond the old 100-row page) in one pass, in well under 5 seconds, while a representative sample of permanently-unresolved rows on both sides of the old page boundary remain durably unresolved rather than hot-looping or being lost. Migration coverage: a new v32->v33 test proves the additive column migration preserves an existing ingress row (defaulting the new column to '', never NULL) and downgraded v28/v29/v30/v26-device-registry fixtures were corrected to also drop telnyx_fax_webhook_events (a table that genuinely did not exist at those legacy versions), fixing a latent 'duplicate column name' migration-test bug the new non-idempotent v32->v33 ALTER surfaced. All pre-existing Phase 1/1.1/2/2.1/3 fax tests unchanged and passing.

Full suite: 413 node:test cases, 412 passed, 1 skipped (opt-in live Twilio, unrelated), 0 failed; vitest App.test.tsx (228 cases) and npm run renderer:build both passed cleanly. No Telnyx network call occurred anywhere in this correction; every signature in server.test.ts's webhook tests was generated locally against a freshly-generated Ed25519 keypair.

RepoPact 2.2.0 validation, LIE-003 schema-ladder invariants (v33 recorded in decisions/0011-schema-migration-coordination.md), and markdown link/last_verified checks all passed after the WI041 ledger updates.

environment.process_note: WI041 Phase 3.1: a focused webhook correctness and retention hardening slice, responding to a GPT-5.6 Sol High review of the actual Phase 3 implementation (schema v32 -> v33). Finding 1: isTelnyxFaxInboundEventType() never listed fax.failed (correctly, since it is not inbound-only), but processTelnyxFaxWebhookEvent() branched routing on that same set rather than on the envelope's own validated direction -- so an authentic inbound fax.failed event fell through into outbound local-fax resolution instead of the deferred_inbound path the frozen contract already documented as correct. Fixed by making event-type/direction compatibility explicit: telnyx-fax-webhook.ts now classifies every supported event type as outbound-only, inbound-only, or shared (fax.failed is the only shared type) via telnyxFaxEventDirectionScope/isTelnyxFaxEventDirectionCompatible, and routing is decided by comparing that scope against the row's validated direction -- an event-type/direction mismatch (e.g. an outbound-only type claiming inbound direction) now fails closed as event_direction_mismatch before any local fax lookup is even attempted, in either direction. Finding 2: parseTelnyxFaxWebhookEnvelope and the ingress queue already carried the bounded failure_category and page_count correctly, but processTelnyxFaxWebhookEvent never forwarded them into recordFaxEvent, and recordFaxEvent itself hardcoded an empty failure_category into the fax_events insert and never passed either field into applyFaxObservation -- silently dropping a known-safe failure reason and never wiring a page_count seam at the canonical fax lifecycle boundary. Fixed by extending FaxEventInput with optional failure_category/page_count, threading them from the ingress row through recordFaxEvent into applyFaxObservation's existing failureCategory/pageCount options (which already existed from Phase 2.1 but were never called with real values here), and always passing the row's own bounded failure_category (never undefined) so a non-failure observation reliably clears rather than preserves a stale prior category. Finding 3: the ingress queue's transient_media_url column had no actual retention bound -- an expired Telnyx signed URL (documented at ~10 minutes for fax.received) could sit in the table indefinitely. Fixed with an additive schema v33 column transient_media_expires_at (computed conservatively from the event's occurred_at plus a cited TELNYX_FAX_TRANSIENT_MEDIA_URL_VALIDITY_MS constant), and a new clearExpiredTelnyxFaxTransientMedia(now) database method that clears only the URL/expiry pair on expired rows -- never the rest of the ingress record, never any fax/document table -- run once at backend startup alongside the existing restart drain. Finding 4: the restart-recovery sweep called unresolvedTelnyxFaxWebhookEvents(100) exactly once, silently truncating at the first 100 rows -- any unresolved backlog beyond that page was permanently unvisited during a given startup, since a still-unresolved row keeps reappearing on that same first page rather than being skipped. Fixed with a new unresolvedTelnyxFaxWebhookEventsPage(afterRowId, limit) using SQLite's own implicit rowid as a stable, monotonically increasing cursor, and server.ts's drainUnresolvedTelnyxFaxWebhookEvents rewritten as a bounded one-pass loop that advances the cursor to every row's own rowid regardless of whether it resolves, terminating as soon as a page comes back empty -- never a continuous poll of the same page. Finding 5: the Phase 3 evidence run (evidence/runs/20260910-fax-phase3-telnyx-fax-webhook-ingress.json) stated timestamp 2026-09-10T20:30:00Z, local clock time mislabeled as UTC, inconsistent with the actual Phase 3 commit (7e65d20, 2026-09-11T01:05:28Z UTC). Corrected in place using the commit timestamp as the documented anchor, with an explicit date_correction note preserving the fact of the original error (matching the precedent set by the Phase 1 evidence date correction) -- the evidence id keeps its original 20260910 local-date filename. FAX-006 was reopened for this review (the inbound fax.failed routing bug meant the original 'the fax-specific event parser/lifecycle correctly handles the frozen event contract' claim was not fully true) and is re-satisfied by this correction together with the original Phase 3 evidence, both retained per the ledger's evidence-preservation rule. FAX-001 through FAX-005 are unaffected. FAX-007 (inbound document acquisition), FAX-009 (document-acquisition amendment), FAX-015, and FAX-016 remain pending and untouched; no inbound document download, camera scanning, cloud acquisition, Fax UI, MCP fax tools, agent governance, or Tauri parity work was attempted in this slice. No live fax was sent, no operator Telnyx credential was used, no live Telnyx resource was mutated, no inbound provider document was downloaded, FAX-007 was not attempted, FAX-009 document acquisition was not implemented, and FAX-016 was not attempted.
